chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Abu Abdillah, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all peace be upon them)

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever enjoins to do good or forbids to do evil or guides to goodness or points towards it is a partner, and whoever orders to do evil, guides one towards evil or points towards it is also a partner.

key_terms.شَرِيك: Partner (one who shares in the reward or punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of someone who guides others to good or evil?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal expands the concept of 'Amr bil-Ma'ruf wa Nahy anil-Munkar' beyond direct action to include guidance and suggestion, establishing a broad chain of moral responsibility. It underscores the Shia principle that indirect participation in good or evil deeds carries equal weight in divine recompense, reinforcing the communal duty of enjoining good. This reflects the scholarly view that intention and facilitation are as significant as execution in the hierarchy of moral acts.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-156 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB)

that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Whoever enjoins to do good or forbids to do evil or guides to goodness or points towards it is a partner in its reward. Whoever orders to do evil, guides one towards evil or points towards it is also a partner in its chastisement.”
